facts.title: Pulitzer Rejected
facts.text: In 1940, he rejected the Pulitzer Prize for The Time of Your Life, stating commerce had no business judging art.
facts.spoken: In 1940, he refused the Pulitzer Prize, saying commerce should not judge art.

facts.text: His calling began when his mother gave him manuscripts in Armenian written by his late father.
facts.spoken: In 1922, finding his father's Armenian writings sparked his calling.

facts.title: The Time of Your Life
facts.text: He wrote this masterpiece in just six days before it triumphed on New York stages.
facts.spoken: He wrote his major play in just six days before triumphing on Broadway.

facts.title: The Oscar
facts.text: His screenplay for The Human Comedy earned him the Academy Award for Best Story in 1943.
facts.spoken: His screenplay for The Human Comedy won the Academy Award for Best Story.

facts.title: Come On-a My House
facts.text: With his cousin Ross Bagdasarian, he turned an Armenian folk song into a hit for Rosemary Clooney.
facts.spoken: In 1951, his take on an Armenian song became a hit for Rosemary Clooney.

facts.title: Ancestral Land
facts.text: He visited Soviet Armenia four times starting in 1935 and traveled to Bitlis in 1964.
facts.spoken: He visited Soviet Armenia four times and traveled to Bitlis in 1964.

facts.text: Upon his death in 1981, his ashes were divided between Ararat Cemetery in Fresno and Yerevan's Komitas Pantheon.
facts.spoken: Upon his death in 1981, his ashes were shared between California and Yerevan.

ytTitle: William Saroyan, the Armenian Writer from Fresno Who Rejected the Pulitzer Prize
ytLead: Born in California to a family from Bitlis, William Saroyan conquered Broadway and Hollywood with his vibrant humanism. From Fresno to the Komitas Pantheon in Yerevan, his work remains a monument of Armenian culture.
